binding_lock: CV_T match (slow transverse target) — fewest passing (37/4000); not simultaneously reachable with CV_L=5.2 (538/4000). CV_T=2.6 at r*/dx>=3 is at the edge of MHAS13-matured's joint reach even with kinetics.
binding_lock_auto: dx/resolution (heuristic mislabel — corrected; r*/dx passed 4000/4000, so resolution was NOT the wall)
interpretation: With D solved on the emulator to hit each CV target, ALL candidates resolve (r*/dx>=3). The wall is CV_T=2.6: only 0.9% of (theta, kinetics) combinations can be driven that slow without blocking, and NONE of those also hit CV_L=5.2 + the dV/dt band. Kinetics helps (P1b: it lowers the CV floor) but is insufficient to reach the slow transverse target jointly with the longitudinal target on a resolved grid. Consistent with the architecture's necessary-but-not-sufficient verdict.
escalation_options: Reconsider whether CV_T=2.6-at-r*/dx>=3 is physical for MHAS13-matured (the architecture's 'change the base model' path) — the Kit-Parker hiPSC 5.2/2.6 targets may need a slower-upstroke base model.
Relax a lock: widen the dV/dt band, or accept CV_T slightly above 2.6, or revisit the 2:1 anisotropy target (cross-construct assumption, 2.1+/-0.8).
Add kinetic axes beyond tau_m (v_half_shift + tau_h/tau_j jointly) with active-learning refill near the CV_T boundary and a larger training budget.

provenance.note: n_training kept modest for a first production run; a larger budget + active learning near the CV_T=2.6 boundary would tighten the verdict.
